title: Reconcile, compare, cut over, and recover
scope: Build synthetic legacy fixture, profiler, source map, ledger, and replayable transformations.
Map verified identities and projects with reviewed evidence; retain ambiguous rows outside target access.
Fence writers, capture deltas, shadow compare, canary one organization, and rehearse compatible rollback.
excluded: Matching project identities by similar names
invariants: Every source association including report refs receives a ledger outcome.
Replay of unchanged snapshot/transform is idempotent.
Each organization has one authoritative writer mode and monotonic epoch.

acceptance.given: Legacy fields disagree on intended access
acceptance.then: review_required with source provenance; no guessed grant and no tenant cutover
acceptance.evidence: ambiguous_access synthetic fixture and ledger evidence

acceptance.given: An active legacy user has no verified issuer/subject mapping
acceptance.then: identity remains in reconciliation and tenant gate is blocked

acceptance.given: A snapshot has nulls, malformed embedded data, unknown resources, locale conflicts, and report refs
acceptance.then: every element is accounted for; second run creates no duplicate target or ledger rows
acceptance.evidence: synthetic reconciliation totals and replay tests

acceptance.given: Legacy unscoped writer can touch users from several organizations
acceptance.then: writer is globally disabled or replaced by a validated scoped adapter before canary

acceptance.given: Shadow decisions differ from reviewed baseline
acceptance.then: unexplained added or removed permissions block cutover, including deny cases

acceptance.given: A target grant is revoked after cutover
acceptance.when: the previous compatible application is deployed
acceptance.then: target authority and revocation remain effective

acceptance.given: Writer deltas remain unapplied or fence drain times out
acceptance.then: tenant stays fenced in the safe prior mode with an explicit recovery action

acceptance.given: A customer manager, ordinary staff, or expired reviewer requests a migration manifest or resolution
acceptance.then: the request is denied; only explicitly authorized unexpired staff reviewers see their organization and a web resolution cannot switch authority
acceptance.evidence: migration_reviewer capability, cross-organization export, and stale review version tests
